photo.title: "Cave of Tong-nab, Tongo Zugu" on reverse.  A natural temple in the form of a large rock cavern is the shrine of the god Tong-Nab. Here is the cave entrance, through which all attending rites enter and leave backwards. [part of an important Talense ceremony held 6 May 1928, at the shrine of Ton-nab [literally the Chief of Ton] in the Tong Hills] Captioned in Rattray, 1932, Figure 76: "We came to the low entrance of the cave".

"Tendana of Tongo Nab of Tongo Zungu" [on reverse] about to sacrifice a sheep at the close of the ceremony. [part of an important Talense ceremony held 6 May 1928, at the shrine of Ton-nab [literally the Chief of Ton] in the Tong Hills]

Head and shoulders profile portrait of "Talense Ten'dan. Tongo". on reverse. [Ten'dana means Chief-Priest or Priest-King, one who is responsible for the settlement of the clan]. He is wearing a string hat, characteristic of holders of this position.

Head and shoulders half profile portrait of "Tendan of Tongo" [on reverse]. [Ten'dana means Chief-Priest or Priest-King, one who is responsible for the settlement of the clan]. He is wearing a string hat, characteristic of holders of this position.

Portrait of three Ten'dama: "Tendan of Tongo". on reverse. Three men dressed in animal skins, wearing string hats characteristic of holders of this position.[Ten'dana means Chief-Priest or Priest-King, one who is responsible for the settlement of the clan].
Hunters of Tongo; full-length view of Talaga and another, with bows, quivers, helmets etc.
"Attending funeral custom. Tongo" on reverse. At a seance attended by Rattray, "the soothsayer then began to rattle ...." Note wand and accessories, hats, bells in background.
Saghelieri, Tongo, sitting near graves
People sitting on stones. Tong Nab [part of an important Talense ceremony held 6 May 1928, at the shrine of Ton-nab [literally the Chief of Ton] in the Tong Hills]

Head and shoulders profile portrait of "Saghelieri, Tendana of Tongo" [on reverse]. Captioned in Rattray, 1932, Frontispiece: "A Ten'dana" [Ten'dana means Chief-Priest or Priest-King, one who is responsible for the settlement of the clan]. He is wearing a string hat, characteristic of holders of this position.

Head and shoulders profile portrait  of a "Tongo man. Talense" [on reverse] named Sayezaa, a section head. A Talensi town, ten, is divided into sections, all the inhabitants of whom trace descent from a common ancestor

Half length profile portrait of a hunter showing arm arrow quiver, facial tribal markings and 'hunting calabash' helmet, bow. 
"Talanga Tongo" [on reverse]

"Saghelieri, Tendana of Tongo" [on reverse].  Inside the compound is a large grain store with a chameleon in bas relief on the side, Sayebere's hand is resting on the chameleon, this is the shrine of his paternal grandmother. At the foot of this are other shrines, seen indistinctly in the photograph

Portrait of "Saghelieri, Tendana of Tongo" [on reverse].  He is seated next to other shrines in Sayebere's compound which are annotated A, B and C. A is the shrine of of the Ten'dan's own mother, Kurug; the actual spirit is the head of a hoe let into the clay; B is a log of wood with a stone on top; C is a pot out of which an infant which has become a ward of a spirit is given to drink [Rattray, 1932, p.355]

Portrait of "Saghelieri, Tendana of Tongo" [on reverse].  He is seated next to other shrines in Saxebere's compound which are annotated A, B and C. A is the shrine of of the Ten'dan's own mother, Kurug; the actual spirit is the head of a hoe let into the clay; B is a log of wood with a stone on top; C is a pot out of which an infant which has become a ward of a spirit is given to drink [Rattray, 1932, p.355]
"Attending funeral custom. Tongo" on reverse. At a seance attended by Rattray, "the soothsayer then began to rattle ...." Note wand and accessories, hats, bells in background.
Despite note on reverse, "Cave of Tong Nab. Zung Zugu", this print appears to be a wider view of the seance depicted in RY.C.23 and 24.
Grave of former chiefs of (Tongo) Talense [on reverse]. Rattray proposes the design of spirit shrines were originally copied from such structures
"Graves of Tongo, Talense". Captioned in Rattray, 1932, Figure 65: "Talense graves".

The Chief of Ten'zugu and the Ten'dan, wearing amulets and fetishes, present at an important Talense ceremony held 6 May 1928, at the shrine of Ton-nab [literally the Chief of Ton] in the Tong Hills. Captioned in Rattray, 1932, Figure 74: "The Chief of Ten'zugu and the Ten'dan' arrived".

"Tong-nab, Tongo Zugu" [on reverse]. As one of the avoidances of the Ton-nab shrine is clothes, those attending rites in connection with its cult must strip: here clothes are piled up and scattered over the boulders [part of an important Talense ceremony held 6 May 1928, at the shrine of Ton-nab [literally the Chief of Ton] in the Tong Hills]

Head and shoulders profile portrait of "Tendan of Wakijiga. Tongo" [on reverse]. [Ten'dana means Chief-Priest or Priest-King, one who is responsible for the settlement of the clan]. He is wearing a string hat, characteristic of holders of this position and has cicatrises on the face.
"Two Talense women. Tongo" [on reverse] standing with an arm around each other's neck, wearing groin covers. Houses in the background
Zung is the compound of Saghelieri, Tongo. Zung is perhaps a transcription of Zon or Zono, hut. Incised building designs.
